test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted idiom.

My friend was **playing the devil’s advocate** in the discussion

options.text: One who is composed at all times
One who pits the culprit against the lawyer
One who argues against something just for the sake of arguing
One who is good at judgement

solution:
The correct answer is "**One who argues against something just for the sake of arguing**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "playing the devil's advocate" means to argue against something for the sake of argument, even if you don't believe in what you're saying.**
 
• "वह जो केवल बहस करने के लिए किसी चीज़ के ख़िलाफ़ बहस करता है।"
 
• The phrase comes from the idea of a person taking on the role of the devil's advocate in a legal proceeding, arguing against the defendant's case to test its strength.
 
 
• Example: I don't really believe all that - I was just playing devil's advocate.
 
 
 
• The friend in this context is not necessarily being malicious or trying to cause trouble, but rather is playing a role to challenge the other person's argument.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3.**
